description: Integrate the full OrgRBAC system from /projects/sandbox/rbac-org into EDMS, replacing the current simple user/role model with UUID-based users, fine-grained resource:action permissions, org structure (units, positions, grades), LDAP support, session cookies, and audit trail. Adapt the rbac-org synchronous PostgreSQL-specific code to work with EDMS's async SQLAlchemy ORM pattern supporting both SQLite and PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL.
steps: Step 1 - Replace app/models/user.py with the full OrgRBAC model set. Create new models adapted to async SQLAlchemy mapped_column pattern (no 'org' schema for SQLite compat, use String(36) for UUIDs instead of PostgreSQL UUID type). Models to create: User (UUID PK, display_name, is_ldap, ldap_dn), Role (UUID PK, code, name, is_system), Permission (UUID PK, resource, action), RolePermission, UserRole (with granted_by, expires_at), OrgUnitType, OrgUnit (tree with parent_id), OrgGrade, OrgPosition, OrgUserGrade, OrgUserAssignment, OrgChangeHistory, LdapConfig, LdapGroupRole, LdapSyncLog. Keep the existing FolderAssignment model for backward compat but update its user FK to UUID string.

Step 2 - Update app/core/config.py to add LDAP settings (LDAP_ENABLED, LDAP_SERVER, LDAP_PORT, LDAP_BASE_DN, LDAP_BIND_DN, LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD), BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME/PASSWORD/EMAIL, and any new settings needed.

Step 3 - Rewrite app/core/security.py to support both Bearer token (API) and session cookie (access_token cookie) auth patterns. Add require_auth, require_role(*roles), and require_permission(resource, action) dependency factories that work with async SQLAlchemy. Keep backward compat with get_current_user for API endpoints. The user dict/object returned from auth deps should include roles list and permissions list.

Step 4 - Create app/services/ldap_service.py adapted from /projects/sandbox/rbac-org/app/services/ldap_service.py but using async SQLAlchemy sessions. Functions: test_connection, run_sync, authenticate_ldap. Handle ldap3 import gracefully (optional dependency).

Step 5 - Create app/api/org.py router with CRUD for org units, positions, grades, user assignments, org chart, and change history. Adapt from /projects/sandbox/rbac-org/app/routers/org.py but use async SQLAlchemy ORM queries instead of raw SQL. Return HTML pages using Jinja2 templates.
Step 6 - Create app/api/rbac.py router with CRUD for roles and permissions. Adapt from /projects/sandbox/rbac-org/app/routers/rbac.py.
Step 7 - Create app/api/ldap.py router with LDAP config CRUD, test connection, sync, and group-role mapping. Adapt from /projects/sandbox/rbac-org/app/routers/ldap.py.
Step 8 - Update app/api/users.py to use the new user model with org structure info (assignments, grades). Update user list/detail/create/edit/delete to work with UUID PKs and new role system.

Step 9 - Update app/api/auth.py to support both API (Bearer token) and HTML form (session cookie) login. Add /login (GET form, POST handler), /logout, /profile pages. Keep /api/auth/* endpoints for API clients.

Step 10 - Create all Jinja2 HTML templates for the new pages: app/templates/org/ (dashboard.html, units.html, positions.html, grades.html, assignments.html, chart.html, history.html), app/templates/rbac/ (roles.html, permissions.html), app/templates/ldap/ (config.html), app/templates/users/ (list.html, form.html, detail.html), app/templates/auth/ (profile.html). Use the existing base.html pattern with Tailwind CSS + htmx.
Step 11 - Update app/main.py lifespan to seed the new roles, permissions, unit types, grades, and bootstrap admin using the async ORM (adapt from /projects/sandbox/rbac-org/app/init_db.py seed data).
Step 12 - Update app/api/router.py to include new routers (org, rbac, ldap).
Step 13 - Update app/models/__init__.py to export all new models.
Step 14 - Update app/api/documents.py and other existing endpoints to use require_permission('documents', 'read') etc. for access control on document operations.

Step 15 - Update existing tests in tests/test_auth.py and tests/test_rbac.py to work with the new model structure. Add new tests for RBAC permission checks, org structure CRUD, and the new auth flows. Update tests/conftest.py fixtures to seed the new role/permission structure.
Step 16 - Add 'ldap3' and 'pycryptodome' as optional dependencies in pyproject.toml.
acceptance_criteria: All new OrgRBAC models (User, Role, Permission, RolePermission, UserRole, OrgUnitType, OrgUnit, OrgGrade, OrgPosition, OrgUserGrade, OrgUserAssignment, OrgChangeHistory, LdapConfig, LdapGroupRole, LdapSyncLog) are defined in app/models/
Auth supports both Bearer token (for API) and session cookie (for HTML pages)
require_role and require_permission dependency factories work correctly
Org structure CRUD (units, positions, grades, assignments) works via HTML pages
RBAC management (roles, permissions) works via HTML pages
LDAP config page exists (functional when ldap3 is installed)
Bootstrap admin is created on startup with full admin role
All existing tests pass plus new tests for RBAC/org features
Running 'uv run pytest tests/ -v' passes all tests
verification: uv run ruff check app/ tests/
findings: All 170 tests pass. Models use String(36) for UUID PKs (SQLite compatible). The old RoleName enum is preserved for backward compat but roles now use code-based strings. UserRole junction table replaces the old user_roles many-to-many table. The User.roles property returns Role objects, User.role_codes returns code strings, User.permissions returns resource:action strings. Auth supports both Bearer token and session cookie. Workflow and annotation models updated to use String(36) FK for user_id. The get_current_user dependency now also accepts a Request parameter to read session cookies.
